data.business: The Group is engaged in the manufacturing, selling, and distribution of paints, coatings, home decor products, bath fittings, modular kitchens, decorative lighting, uPVC doors and windows, and related services (0.37). It earns revenue predominantly through sales to dealers and distributors, which accounted for 99.0% of total sales in FY 2025-26 (0.24). In addition, the company generates revenue via its network of 74 Beautiful Home Stores and industrial joint ventures providing coatings for auto OE and general industrial products (1.2, 2.4).
data.narrative: The annual report portrays a stable business with 4.10% standalone revenue growth, strong liquidity, and continued investments in R&T facilities and capital expenditures (0.11, 0.12, 0.13, 0.23, 0.26, 0.44). Management on recent earnings calls agrees on this operational strength, highlighting an all-time high gross margin of about 45.6% in the fourth quarter and a full-year consolidated margin of 18.8% (2.1, 2.18). However, call commentary shifts focus toward headwind management, emphasizing strong competitive intensity and persistent discounting across retailers, raw material dependence on crude, and currency devaluation challenges in Ethiopia (1.3, 1.8, 1.15, 2.12). Management also places greater emphasis on proactive pricing actions, such as cumulative price increases of 10.5% to 11%, and manufacturing execution like the operational white cement plant in Fujairah (1.1, 2.13).

bull.point: Margins and pricing power demonstrated resilience, with gross margins reaching an all-time high of about 45.6% in Q4 and full-year consolidated margins finishing at 18.8% after cumulative price hikes of 10.5% to 11% (2.1, 2.13, 2.18).

The company continues to expand its retail footprint, growing to over 1.6 lakh retail outlets with more than 6,000 retail touchpoints added in FY26 while engaging over 137,000 business influencers (0.3, 2.2, 3.1).

Product innovation and capacity projects are advancing, as new products generate 16% of overall revenues, the white cement plant in Fujairah is fully operational, and the VAM-VAE backward integration project progresses (1.1, 1.13, 3.2).
Asian Paints delivered strong shareholder returns, declaring total dividends of Rs. 27.5 per share for the year, representing a 60% payout ratio (2.10).

bear.point: Competitive intensity remains strong across economy, premium, and luxury segments, marked by persistent discounting across retailers and contractors (1.15, 2.12).
The business faces input and macro vulnerabilities, including high dependence on crude and crude derivatives as well as currency devaluation challenges in Ethiopia (1.3, 1.8).
Performance was impacted by exceptional charges, including a Rs. 94 crore impairment in White Teak and a Rs. 63.74 crore labour code impact (3.10).

The company is exposed to ongoing regulatory and financial risks, including proceedings before the Competition Commission of India along with market, liquidity, and interest rate risks (0.15, 0.32, 0.42).

data.balance: As of 31st March 2026, the company held long-term borrowings of ₹805.42 crores, with ₹771.43 crores hypothecated as security (0.10, 0.39). Standalone cash, bank balances, term deposits, and mutual funds stood at ₹9,014.60 crores, contributing to a total Group liquidity position of ₹9,762.11 crores, while complete cash flow statements were not provided (0.11, 0.44).
